summary: Promote existing Sven Beckert roster identity to the main timeline with six dated works/interviews and three scoped contributions. Add The Monied Metropolis to urban history and a first-person global-method strand; retain the existing capitalism debate and its critics. Capitalism (2025) is metadata only.
authorization: User explicitly identified Beckert as missing from the live main timeline. Coordinator assigned this bounded 1.169 packet on baseline 1.168. Packet preparation and review only; coordinator applies the canonical change. No publication requested.
rationale: Roster and named-work reading coverage did not supply an individual main-timeline entry. Selected author passages and interviews ground substantial content separately from dissertation frequency. Existing identities, collective arrows, critical qualifications and field coverage are preserved.

strand.title: Urban elites and the formation of a bourgeoisie
strand.focus: Beckert makes the coherence of New York’s capital-owning elites a historical question. Institutions, cultural boundaries and political conflicts help explain how a shared class identity was made. This selected introduction adds an urban elite-formation problem alongside existing histories of neighbourhoods, mobility and racial inequality; it does not replace them.

strand.title: Capitalism as connected regional diversity
strand.focus: In his 2020 methodological answer Beckert relates regional differences and connections: merchants, plantations, manufacturing and state power belong in the same global inquiry. His account resists treating Europe’s industrialisation as the whole history of capitalism. This strand records his stated strategy; the empirical adequacy of its global applications and criticism of the cotton argument remain open.
strand.works: GrowthPolicy interview with Devjani Roy (2020), answer 2; Empire of Cotton (2014, existing limited excerpt)
